1.note: Ezekiel is using the phrase translated as **And it happened** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

1.q: בְּ⁠אַחַ֤ת עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה בַּ⁠שְּׁלִישִׁ֖י בְּ⁠אֶחָ֣ד לַ⁠חֹ֑דֶשׁ
1.note: If your language would not represent numbers in forms such as **eleventh**, **third**, and **first**, you could represent these numbers in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [in year eleven, in month three, on day one of the month]

The **third** month of the Hebrew calendar includes the end of May and the beginning of June on Western calendars. You could convert the Hebrew day and month into an approximate date on the calendar that your culture uses. However, the Jews used a lunar calendar, so if you use a solar calendar, the date will be different every year, and the translation will not be entirely accurate. So you may just want to give the number of the day and the name of the month on the Hebrew calendar and say in a footnote approximately what time of year that is on your calendar.
See how you translated this expression in [6:1](ta:06).

2.note: See how you translated **Son of man** in [2:1](ta:02).

Yahweh is using the question form to introduce a comparison between Pharaoh and the great nation that he is about to describe. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Consider whom you are like in your greatness.]

The word **you** is singular here because Yahweh is addressing Pharaoh, even though he is also speaking to **his multitude**. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **greatness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [in how great you are]

3.note: Yahweh is speaking as if Assyria were **a cedar in Lebanon**. It means that Assyria was a great and powerful nation, just as a cedar in Lebanon was a very large and impressive tree. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Behold, Assyria was as great and impressive as a cedar in Lebanon]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **cedar** that is characterized by a beautiful **branch** and by great **height**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [with beautiful branches … and very tall]

Yahweh is speaking as if the cedar were **a forest giving shade**. It means that its branches were so thick and spread out so widely that it gave as much shade as a whole forest. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and with branches so thick and wide that they gave as much shade as a whole forest]

4.note: Yahweh is speaking of **Waters** and **the deep** as if they were living things that could raise the tree and make it grow tall. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [It grew great because of the waters; it grew high because of the deep]

The implication is that **the deep** refers to the waters deep under the ground that supplied springs and rivers. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the deep waters under the ground]

4.q: אֶת נַהֲרֹתֶ֗י⁠הָ הֹלֵךְ֙ סְבִיב֣וֹת מַטָּעָ֔⁠הּ וְ⁠אֶת תְּעָלֹתֶ֣י⁠הָ שִׁלְחָ֔ה
4.note: The pronoun **its** in **its rivers** and **its channels** and the pronoun **it** refer to **the deep**, but **its** in **its planting** refers to the cedar tree. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [with the rivers of the deep going around where the cedar was planted, and the deep sent out its channels]

5.note: The word translated as **Therefore** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [As a result]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [because of the many waters that the deep sent out to it]

6.q: בִּ⁠סְעַפֹּתָ֤י⁠ו קִֽנְנוּ֙ כָּל ע֣וֹף הַ⁠שָּׁמַ֔יִם וְ⁠תַ֤חַת פֹּֽארֹתָי⁠ו֙ יָֽלְד֔וּ כֹּ֖ל חַיַּ֣ת הַ⁠שָּׂדֶ֑ה
6.note: Yahweh is speaking of the peoples who were ruled by Assyria as if they were birds that **nested in its limbs** and beasts that **gave birth under its boughs**. It means that many peoples lived under the rule of Assyria and depended on it. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Peoples of every kind lived under the rule of Assyria and depended on it]

Yahweh is speaking as if the protection and rule of Assyria were **its shade**. It means that many nations lived under the protection and control of Assyria, just as people rest in the shade of a large tree. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and all of the many nations lived under its protection and control]

7.note: If your language does not use nouns for the ideas of **greatness** and **length**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [in how great it was and in how long its branches were]

7.q: כִּֽי הָיָ֥ה שָׁרְשׁ֖⁠וֹ אֶל מַ֥יִם רַבִּֽים
7.note: Yahweh is speaking as if the abundant resources of Assyria were **many waters** that fed **its root**. It means that Assyria had plenty of resources that made it strong and prosperous, just as a tree that has plenty of water grows large. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [for it had plenty of resources that made it strong]

8.note: Yahweh is using **did not darken it** as a common expression of the culture to mean “did not overshadow it,” that is, the other cedars were not greater than it. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Cedars in the garden of God were not greater than it]

8.q: בְּרוֹשִׁ֗ים לֹ֤א דָמוּ֙ אֶל סְעַפֹּתָ֔י⁠ו וְ⁠עַרְמֹנִ֥ים לֹֽא הָי֖וּ כְּ⁠פֹֽארֹתָ֑י⁠ו
8.note: Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [the limbs of cypresses were not like its limbs, and the boughs of plane trees were not like its boughs]

The term **plane trees** refers to a kind of large tree with broad leaves and wide-spreading branches. If your readers would not be familiar with what plane trees are, you could use the name of a similar tree that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [and large spreading trees]

9.note: If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **abundance**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [with its many branches]

9.q: וַ⁠יְקַנְאֻ֨⁠הוּ֙ כָּל עֲצֵי עֵ֔דֶן אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּ⁠גַ֥ן הָ⁠אֱלֹהִֽים
9.note: Yahweh is speaking of **all the trees of Eden** as if they were living things that could feel envy. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and it was so beautiful that it seemed as though all the trees of Eden that were in the garden of God envied it]

10.note: See how you translated this expression in 5:7.

Yahweh is speaking as if the greatness of Assyria were the **height** of a tree. It means that Assyria had become very great and powerful. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Because it became very great]

Yahweh is speaking as if Assyria were a tree that **set its top among the thick boughs**. It means that Assyria exalted itself above the other nations. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and it exalted itself above the other nations]

Yahweh is speaking as if being proud were having a **heart** that **was high**. It means that Assyria became arrogant because it was so great. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and it became proud because it was so great]

11.note: The word translated as **and** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes this clear. Alternate translation: [therefore I gave it]
Here, **hand** represents “power” or “control.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [into the control]

The implication is that **a mighty one of the nations** refers to the king of Babylon. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the king of Babylon, a mighty one of the nations]

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb translated as **doing** and **did** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [he dealt with it severely]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **wickedness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Because of how wickedly it acted]

12.q: וַ⁠יִּכְרְתֻ֧⁠הוּ זָרִ֛ים עָרִיצֵ֥י גוֹיִ֖ם וַֽ⁠יִּטְּשֻׁ֑⁠הוּ אֶל־הֶ֠⁠הָרִים וּ⁠בְ⁠כָל־גֵּ֨אָי֜וֹת נָפְל֣וּ דָלִיּוֹתָ֗י⁠ו וַ⁠תִּשָּׁבַ֤רְנָה פֹֽארֹתָי⁠ו֙ בְּ⁠כֹל֙ אֲפִיקֵ֣י הָ⁠אָ֔רֶץ וַ⁠יֵּרְד֧וּ מִ⁠צִּלּ֛⁠וֹ כָּל־עַמֵּ֥י הָ⁠אָ֖רֶץ וַֽ⁠יִּטְּשֻֽׁ⁠הוּ
12.note: Yahweh is speaking as if the conquest of Assyria were the felling of a tree when he says that foreign soldiers **cut it down**. It means that ruthless foreign armies conquered and destroyed Assyria. **Its branches** and **boughs** may represent the collapse and scattering of the Assyrian armies that were garrisoned around the empire to preserve order and stability. He is also speaking of the nations who had been under Assyrian protection as if they were birds and animals that **went down from** the great tree’s **shade**. It means that the peoples who had depended on the king of Assyria for protection and security left him when he was defeated. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And strangers, the ruthless of the nations, conquered and destroyed it. Its armies were scattered in the mountains, valleys, and channels of the land. And all the peoples of the land left the protection of the empire and abandoned it.]
See how you translated this phrase in 28:7.

The expression **were broken** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. The **strangers** mentioned earlier in the verse are the ones who did this action. Alternate translation: [and the strangers broke its boughs in all the channels of the land]

13.q: עַל מַפַּלְתּ֥⁠וֹ יִשְׁכְּנ֖וּ כָּל ע֣וֹף הַ⁠שָּׁמָ֑יִם וְ⁠אֶל פֹּארֹתָ֣י⁠ו הָי֔וּ כֹּ֖ל חַיַּ֥ת הַ⁠שָּׂדֶֽה
13.note: Yahweh is speaking of the nations that took advantage of the downfall of Assyria as if they were birds and beasts that settled on **its ruin**. It means that other nations profited from Assyria after it was destroyed. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Every nation would take advantage of Assyria after its ruin, and all the peoples would profit from what remained of it]

14.q: לֹא יִגְבְּה֨וּ בְ⁠קוֹמָתָ֜⁠ם כָּל עֲצֵי מַ֗יִם
14.note: Yahweh is speaking as if other nations and their rulers were **trees of waters**, that is, trees that have plenty of water. It means that no other nation would become as great and proud as Assyria had been. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [all the prosperous nations will not become so great and proud]

The implication is that even the mightiest of these trees, which represent the most powerful nations, will not proudly rise up to a great height as the cedar did. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and their mighty ones will not stand proudly in their height as the cedar did]

Yahweh is speaking as if prosperous nations were trees that are **drinkers of waters**. It means that these nations had plenty of resources and were strong, just as trees that have plenty of water grow large. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [all of the nations that had abundant resources]

The expression **have been given** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Yahweh is the one who has done this. Alternate translation: [For I have given all of them to death]
See how you translated the similar expression **son of man** in [2:1](ta:02).
See how you translated the similar expression in 26:20.

Yahweh is using **the ones going down to the pit** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the people who die and are buried.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to the people who die and are buried]

15.note: Yahweh is using **In the day of** as a common expression of the culture to mean “At the time of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [When it went down to Sheol]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **mourning**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [I caused people to mourn]

The expression **were restrained** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Yahweh is the one who did this. Alternate translation: [and I restrained many waters]

Yahweh is speaking as if causing Lebanon to mourn were making it **dark**, like a person dressed in dark mourning clothes. It means that Yahweh caused Lebanon to mourn deeply over the fall of Assyria. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I caused Lebanon to grieve deeply over it]

Yahweh is speaking as if people were **trees of the field** who could be **faint**. It means that the people groups who flourished in the Assyrian empire became weak because Assyria had fallen. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and all the trees of the field drooped because of it] or [and all the dependent peoples despaired]

16.note: Yahweh is speaking as if the news of the defeat of Assyria were like the loud crash of a great tree falling. It means that when the nations heard that Assyria had been destroyed, they were terrified. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I made nations tremble with terror when they heard that Assyria had been destroyed]

Yahweh is speaking as if the other nations were **trees of Eden** who could be **comforted** after suffering a loss. It means that the other great nations, which had already collapsed, felt consoled when they saw the great tree, Assyria, brought down to join them in the lower land. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And all the other nations were consoled]

The expression **were comforted** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. The text does not say who comforted these trees, so you could say that they found comfort. Alternate translation: [And … took comfort]
See how you translated the similar expression in 26:20.

The terms **choicest** and **good** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [the very best trees of Lebanon]

Yahweh is using the adjectives **choicest** and **good** as nouns to mean the best trees. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate these adjectives with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [the very best trees of Lebanon] or [the very best of the other nations]
See how you translated the similar expression in 31:14.

17.note: The pronoun **They** refers to all the trees of Eden mentioned in the previous verse, which represent other nations. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Those trees of Eden also, with it, went down to Sheol] or [Those other nations went down to Sheol with Assyria]

Here, **the sword** represents “battle.” The phrase **the slain of the sword** refers to people who were killed in war. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to those who were killed in battle]

Here, **its arm** represents “its strength,” referring to the allies who gave it military strength. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and its military allies]

Yahweh is speaking as if the nations were birds or animals that **dwelt in its shade**, the shade of a great tree. It means that the nations lived under the protection and power of Assyria, the great tree. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the ones who had lived safely under its power in the midst of the nations]

18.q: אֶל מִ֨י דָמִ֥יתָ כָּ֛כָה בְּ⁠כָב֥וֹד וּ⁠בְ⁠גֹ֖דֶל בַּ⁠עֲצֵי עֵ֑דֶן
18.note: Yahweh is using the question form to mock Pharaoh for thinking that none of **the trees of Eden** is as glorious and great as he is. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You think that none of the trees of Eden is like you in glory and in greatness!]

The terms **glory** and **greatness** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [in such great splendor]

Yahweh uses the word **But** here to indicate a contrast between how great Pharaoh thinks he is and the humiliation that he will experience. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Yet in reality you will be brought down]

The expression **will be brought down** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Yahweh is the one who will do this. Alternate translation: [But I will bring you down]
See how you translated the similar expression in 26:20.

The implication is that to **lie down in the midst of the uncircumcised** was to die a shameful death, since people who were not circumcised were unclean and outside of God’s covenant. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [In disgrace and estranged from God, in the midst of the uncircumcised]

Yahweh is referring to death in a polite way by using the phrase **lie down**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [you will die and lie dead with the slain of the sword]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [That is what will happen to Pharaoh and all of his multitude]
See how you translated **the declaration of the Lord Yahweh** in 30:6.
